messages:
sasha: Heads-up: I saw a 3x tail-latency spike on the FIFO KV policy when running long-context streams (100k tokens). Memory for the KV pool climbs steadily and we hit paging, then latency explodes. Repro steps below.

alex_r: repro?

sasha: yes — local stress harness: `./tools/kv_stress --policy=fifo --seq=100000 --clients=64 --batch=auto` — run with `--log-allocs` to see reinserts.

kevin: can you paste the alloc log snippet?

sasha: pasted small excerpt:
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:01Z] evict candidate node=0x7f9a4 size=512k age=120
[2026-03-10T14:12:01Z] reinserting key=0x7f9a4 at tail (fifo)
[2026-03-10T14:12:01Z] evict candidate node=0x7f9a4 size=512k age=121
[2026-03-10T14:12:01Z] reinserting key=0x7f9a4 at tail (fifo)
[... repeated hundreds of times ...]
```
This keeps the same node live but never lets other entries get promoted; looks like a reinsertion loop under contention.

tina: that sounds like the classic FIFO reinsertion where we move node to tail even if it's being evicted concurrently. If evict and reinstate race you can end up thrashing. Did you try LRU?

sasha: LRU test didn't show the same memory growth; peak mem was 40% lower and no paging.

kevin: interesting. Can you share pprof CPU and heap snapshots from the run?

sasha: uploaded: `/tmp/prof/fifo_cpu.pb.gz` and `/tmp/prof/fifo_heap.pb.gz`. Quick diff: CPU shows heavy time in `kv::evict_if_needed` and `mutex::lock` in the FIFO path; heap histogram shows many large slab allocations pinned by 'in_reinsert' flag.

perf-bot: flamegraph: https://perf/reports/1843123456/fifo-flame.html (shows hotspot at kv::try_reinsert -> evict loop) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex_r: thanks. Hypothesis: under high concurrency, `try_reinsert` uses a spin-and-insert that can requeue the same node repeatedly because the eviction check uses a non-atomic age counter. We should add a reinsertion backoff or check ownership bit.

kevin: agree — two fixes to try: 1) make reinsertion conditional on a CAS on node->state so concurrent evictions don't flip it back repeatedly; 2) add a per-shard eviction budget to prevent single-key thrash. Which is simpler to roll?

tina: CAS on node->state is low-risk and should fix correctness. Budgeting will help perf but is more invasive (shard accounting, metrics).

sasha: implemented CAS prototype (branch: `kv/fifo-reinsert-cas`) — local runs look promising: no reinsertion loop, memory growth bounded. I still see small latency blips when kernel selection switches between int8 and fp16 for big attention kernels — probably unrelated but worth noting.

kevin: good. Can you add regression test in `runtime/tests/kv_repro` that runs the harness for 30s with REPEAT=100 and asserts no more than X% mem growth? Also add a unit test that verifies CAS prevents double-reinsert.

sasha: on it. One more observation: batching heuristics interact — when batch=auto we saw more reinserts because long sequences got split across batches and produced overlapping KV footprints. Setting `--batch=max_tokens=2048` reduced overlap and thrash. So we should consider a heuristic: avoid splitting sequences across batches if it would produce >N% KV overlap.

alex_r: that's a good systems-level signal. Might be worth an optimizer pass: when scheduling batches, compute predicted KV window overlap using prefix lengths and avoid splitting hot streams. Create a ticket for that.

infra-bot: created ticket #INF-2184 "KV FIFO reinsertion CAS + batch overlap heuristic" and linked branch `kv/fifo-reinsert-cas`.

kevin: plan: 1) land CAS fix + tests (hotfix branch) 2) add stress job to CI that runs FIFO stress overnight on dedicated infra 3) follow up with batching heuristic RFC.

sasha: ok i'll open PR today for the CAS and tests, include perf snapshots and flamegraph links in PR body. Thanks for the triage! :thumbsup:
